name: judging room, 3 minutes, one laptop
notes: space = next beat, b = back, r = restart. Replays are real runs from crew/exports, labelled REPLAY · Nx on screen. The live beat switches the Stage to runs/live without a reload. 'say' is the speaker's line (docs/MESSAGING.md); it is never shown on screen.

beats.say: 87% of classic games are endangered, and most of their source code is gone. Lost games, rebuilt and proven.
Doom is our first patient. Muse writes it. Snap judges it. The compiler proves it. Every green cell is a piece of Doom proved byte for byte. This is a real run, at 8x.
Agents lie. The referee doesn't. Every claim is re-run by the compiler, and two labs screen every match for fakes.
Counts, not vibes: functions proved out of all of Doom. Violet with a question mark is our guess; everything else is proved.
This part is live. Play it, and we rebuild it: the crew is working on Doomguy's face right now.
Every game we bring back makes the next one faster. Same model, same budget: these are the numbers, per run.
Emulators keep games playable. Source code keeps them alive. It's alive.
Built today, and what's not ours. Games don't have to die.
